question: Should shared message paths fail closed by deleting all `channelData` when any opaque key or value contains protected runtime context, while rejecting malformed string payloads at JSON normalization?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but this choice intentionally trades channel-native payload preservation and legacy tolerance for a stricter outbound security boundary; repository history does not establish that permanent contract without an owner decision.

options.title: Approve fail-closed contract
options.body: Keep whole-payload rejection for protected content and object-only JSON normalization, then merge after rebasing and green exact-head checks.

options.title: Preserve broader compatibility
options.body: Revise normalization to retain the prior malformed-string behavior or define a narrower rejection rule, with explicit regression coverage for the chosen legacy contract.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Keep current behavior until a narrower channelData schema or owner-specific payload contract can make filtering deterministic.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed contract
recommendation.body: Keep whole-payload rejection for protected content and object-only JSON normalization, then merge after rebasing and green exact-head checks.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commits show the strongest ownership of the shared source-reply, message-tool, and outbound-runner contract being changed.
